keys.statement: Across the Pfizer, GSK and Sanofi guides, water, n-propyl and isopropyl acetate and 1- and 2-butanol are rated green, while chlorinated solvents, NMP, DMF, DMAc, benzene, hexane, 1,4-dioxane and diethyl ether are undesirable.

plain.title: Choosing a solvent or entrainer: start from the green list of the pharmaceutical guides
plain.when: You choose a solvent or entrainer and want to avoid health, safety and environmental problems.
plain.do: Prefer solvents rated green across the Pfizer, GSK and Sanofi guides: water, n-propyl and isopropyl acetate, 1- and 2-butanol. Justify any undesirable one: chlorinated solvents, NMP, DMF and DMAc (polar aprotic solvents), benzene, hexane, 1,4-dioxane, diethyl ether.
plain.why: The solvents' health, safety and environmental ratings differ widely.
plain.check: NMP and DMF, rated undesirable here, are the extractive solvents studied in Li et al. 2017: report the trade-off if a case uses them.

decisions.mechanism: Health, safety and environmental ratings differ widely.
decisions.operation: Prefer the green list; justify any undesirable solvent.
limits: NMP and DMF, rated undesirable here, are the extractive solvents studied in Li 2017; a trade-off to report, not a contradiction of results.
Lab's paraphrase of the source; checked against the locator by the writing AI session only, not by a person.

verification_required: An AI review session checks the statement against byrne-2016-solvent-selection-guides, Unified guides, pp. 8-9 (Figs. 6-7).

keys.statement: Where an ether solvent is needed, 2-methyltetrahydrofuran and tert-butyl methyl ether are preferred to tetrahydrofuran and diethyl ether.

plain.title: Need an ether solvent: use 2-methyltetrahydrofuran or tert-butyl methyl ether
plain.when: A process needs an ether solvent and tetrahydrofuran or diethyl ether are candidates.
plain.do: Use 2-methyltetrahydrofuran or tert-butyl methyl ether instead of tetrahydrofuran and diethyl ether.
plain.why: Safer ethers exist that do a similar job (Byrne et al. 2016).
plain.check: Check with the property method that the substitute gives the solubility and phase behaviour you need.

decisions.obstacle: Ether solvents with poor hazard profiles.
decisions.mechanism: Safer ethers exist with similar function.
limits: Lab's paraphrase of the source; checked against the locator by the writing AI session only, not by a person.

verification_required: An AI review session checks the statement against byrne-2016-solvent-selection-guides, Unified guides, p. 9.

keys.statement: Whether to recover a waste solvent by distillation or incinerate it depends on the energy embodied in making it: recovering tetrahydrofuran saves energy, while diethyl ether is better incinerated.

plain.title: Recover a used solvent or burn it: compare the recovery energy with the energy of making it
plain.when: You decide the fate of a waste solvent.
plain.do: Compare the energy of recovering it by distillation with the energy embodied in producing it. Tetrahydrofuran is worth recovering; diethyl ether is better incinerated.
plain.why: The energy needed to produce a solvent differs strongly between solvents.
plain.check: Estimate the recovery column's duty per kg of solvent and compare it with the production energy from a tool such as the ETH tool described by Byrne et al. 2016.

decisions.mechanism: Production energy differs strongly between solvents.
decisions.operation: Compare recovery energy with production energy.
